text: The buy-back step adds no REST operation of its own. Its surface is the two asset reads it serves, the approval child workflow on rwb-decision, the template price read of rwb-comms, the rwb-deviation raise on the Ownership Map path POST /cases/{caseId}/deviations of /api/recovery/deviation/v1, and the case-move answer to rwb-case, each consumed with a placeholder until its owner confirms the name.
why: No source publishes an operation that opens a buy-back or names the consumed operations, and the legacy endpoint list names only the asset read and the pricing story's listing operation.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-032 Endpoints table; Ownership Map API rows; TSD S5 T-A.1; Architecture v5 slide 19 IN and OUT; API Specification v4
confirm: The owners of rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-decision and rwb-comms at the baseline review, with the tech lead of rwb-asset
impact: If an owner publishes a different name or path, the consumed row, its fake and its client change and the application story is rebuilt against the new document; no rule and no business value changes.

text: The buy-back terms are written on asset_sale with listing_id pointing at the buy-back listing and sale_price taken from the template price reference with its template version, while start_price and floor_price of the listing carry the price the template gives; no table and no column are added, and the template price field and its read operation stay with P6.
why: The rules name a governed template price but no source gives it a field identifier or names the table that holds it, and the template belongs to P6 rwb-comms.
read: TSD S5 T3.1 listing and asset_sale; Ownership Map table rows; Business Rules v4 R-DIS-24 and R-DIS-61; FSD S5 A2.23.3.2
confirm: The owner of rwb-comms and the data steward at the baseline review
impact: If the price belongs to a table or column the sources do not name, the writer, the element and the DB story change together; the rule and the approval path are unaffected.

text: The approval the limit requires is the kit's approval child workflow on rwb-decision, and the limit behind it is a delegated-authority row of rwb-access read at its version. No limit value, percentage or threshold is written in code, in a test or in a fixture, and this service neither decides the approval nor reads the authority table.
why: The legacy criterion and VR-S5-023-1 require the approval the limit requires and give no limit, the delegated-authority table is P4's and the approval is P7's.
read: Legacy AC1; FSD S5 A2.23.3.1; Business Rules v4 R-DIS-24; Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41; Ownership Map
confirm: The owner of rwb-decision with the owner of rwb-access
impact: If the approval is a REST call rather than a child workflow, one client and one fake change; if the limit is published as a parameter, it is read at its version and still never written in code.

text: The buy-back listing is written with sale_channel and status read as reference data at their version, and the buy-back channel value and the buy-back listing status value are Not specified in the source documents, so the build carries the placeholder and adds no value to LOV-SALE-CHANNEL or LOV-LISTING. The asset holding status is left unchanged by this step.
why: Both lists are closed and neither carries a buy-back value, and no source says whether an approved buy-back moves the holding status of the asset.
read: TSD S5 T3.1 listing columns; TSD S5 T3.2 lists; FSD S5 A2.23.3.2; legacy RWB-E4-032 Data
confirm: The owner of the reference data with the tech lead of rwb-asset
impact: If a buy-back value is published, the row and the element carry it and no code changes; if the holding status must move, the listing story's transition owns it and this step is unchanged.

text: The buy-back is agreed from the route-with-approver point of R-DIS-24 while the asset is held: the step reads the case state and the route on the rwb-case contract, requires ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER with the buy-back route, and answers ROUTE_APPROVED_BUYBACK. The case fake returns ASSET_HELD for the asset and ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER for the route, and the two are not the same state.
why: Legacy AC1 gives no from state, R-DIS-24 starts at ROUTE_WITH_APPROVER, and the legacy criterion and the FSD describe the asset as held when the buy-back is opened.
read: Legacy AC1; Business Rules v4 R-DIS-19, R-DIS-20 and R-DIS-24; TSD S5 T4; FSD S5 A2.23.4.1
confirm: The owner of rwb-case with the owner of rwb-decision
impact: If the case must be at another state when the step runs, the guard, the fake and the answer change and the rule row is re-read; the terms and the approval path are unaffected.

text: The former owner is represented by the sale officer acting on the case, and enters this story only as a party key the owner's contract answers. No customer or borrower role, no customer screen and no external edge is added, and the buy-back is signed by the approver the limit names and not by the former owner inside the Workbench.
why: The FSD lists the customer as an also-user, the rights matrix has no customer role, and the architecture states that customers and partners reach the bank only through the partner gateway.
read: FSD S5 A2.23.3.3; TSD S5 T6.1; Architecture v5 slide 20; Ownership Map
confirm: The owner of rwb-access with the sales business owner
impact: If a customer channel is required, it is a partner gateway story and an access story, and this step still writes the listing, the terms and the record unchanged.

text: Both stories trace to REQ-S5-010 of the program and of the FSD, that a transfer to the asset management company, a buy-back and a rental each follow a recorded approval, and the absence of a plan requirement row is carried in the registers instead of being filled with an invented id.
why: The split plan carries an empty requirement list for this key and the program and the FSD both give the requirement.
read: Business Requirements Program v4 REQ-S5-010; FSD S5 requirements served; split plan requirement rows
confirm: The traceability manager with the business analyst
impact: If the plan later allocates a requirement id, the trace row is renumbered and the register row is closed; no acceptance criterion changes.

text: The baseline declares the buy-back as an element of the Asset answer and as rows of listing and asset_sale, and the four consumed rows as consumed with the placeholder, its owner and a faked answer. It declares no operation that opens a buy-back, adds no value to any closed list, and never declares another service's operation, table or topic as its own.
why: No source publishes a buy-back operation, a buy-back channel value or the consumed operation names, so an invented operation would be a value the sources do not carry.
read: Legacy Endpoints table; Ownership Map API rows; TSD S5 T-A.1 and T3.2; Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41
confirm: The consumers of the baseline at the review, and the solution architect
impact: If an owner publishes an operation for the buy-back, the baseline gains one operation and one error set and the application story binds to it; the element and the lists stay as declared.

text: The approval and template fakes are derived from the owners' published documents and carry the placeholder where a field or an operation is not given; the drift test compares each fake with the document, and the template is the P6 rwb-comms table and not a rwb-document table.
why: The approval answer and the template price element are not published, and the Ownership Map places the template with P6.
read: Architecture v5 slide 19 OUT; Ownership Map table rows; TSD S5 T3.1; Business Rules v4 R-DIS-24
confirm: The owners of rwb-decision and rwb-comms
impact: If an owner publishes the shape, the fake and the row are re-derived from it and the drift test keeps them aligned; no business rule changes.

text: The asset row is S5's in schema rwb_asset, read from Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 and TSD S5 T3.1, and the omission of the row from the Ownership Map table list is carried in the register and corrected in the map's next version rather than read as another owner's table.
why: The map lists only listing and asset_sale for S5 while the architecture and the TSD define the asset object in the same schema and the step reads it.
read: Ownership Map table rows; Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41; TSD S5 T3.1
confirm: The solution architect and the data steward
impact: If the map is corrected to another owner, the DB story and the read change with it; the buy-back writes no asset column, so the step's behaviour is unchanged.
